keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox "c. 4400-3800 BC", "Middle and Late Chalcolithic period in the Southern Levant"; the Golan belongs to a separate "Golanian" phase and is left out. No area figure to compare.

ledger.note: 4400 BCE: the Ghassulian Chalcolithic, with its copper hoards and underground dwellings, succeeds the Wadi Rabah. Infobox "c. 4400-3800 BC"; "Preceded by: Wadi Rabah culture"; "the typical later Ghassulian began sometime around the mid-5th millennium"; Beersheba, "where elaborate underground dwellings have been excavated".

region.text: "today's Jordan, Israel and Palestinian territories": Teleilat el-Ghassul "in the eastern Jordan Valley near the northern edge of the Dead Sea", "especially in the region of Beersheba", settlements "in the northern and western Negev", the Chalcolithic Temple of Ein Gedi

ledger.note: 3800 BCE: the Ghassulian ends; the Early Bronze Age I of Canaan follows, which no dossier draws. "the typical later Ghassulian began sometime around the mid-5th millennium and ended ca. 3800 BC"; the transition to EB I "ca. 3800-3500 BC" is flagged as dubious on the page; infobox "Followed by: Early Bronze Age (Canaan)". [Reviewer xx-01-a, 2026-10-18: the page's lead dates the culture "c. 4400 - c. 3500 BC" against the infobox's 3800 BC; the infobox end is kept]

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: a band along the Jordan and radii around Beersheba, Teleilat Ghassul and the coastal plain, never a frontier.

sources.title: Ghassulian
sources.note: Dates 4400-3800 BC, the Jordan valley and Beersheba sites, the Negev, the Golanian exclusion, the EB I transition.

notes: Culture dossier, one page (budget for a new state with no shapes). The southern Levant between 3800 BCE and Cliopatria's first Levantine rows (Ebla from 3000 BCE) is nobody's land: the Early Bronze Age I-II of Canaan has no dossier (gap, out of this group's 6000-3400 scope). Gazetteer: Teleilat Ghassul, Ein Gedi, Nahal Mishmar are not places; Beer Sheva, Amman, Jericho, Tel Aviv radii and the Jordan band stand in. End disagreement (reviewer xx-01-a): infobox c. 3800 BC vs lead c. 3500 BC; 3800 is used.
